newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Fatal virus in Malaysia claims 27th child victim.
newsitem.headline: Fatal virus in Malaysia claims 27th child victim.

text.p: A mysterious airborne virus has killed another small child in Malaysia, the 27th victim of a disease that has baffled medical experts around the world, Malaysian Health Minister Chua Jui Meng said on Monday.

A one-year-old boy from a rural district of Malaysia's Borneo state of Sarawak died of viral myocarditis four hours after being admitted to hospital on Sunday night, the national news agency Bernama quoted Chua as telling reporters.
All of the victims have been children in Sarawak and all have died of viral myocarditis, or heart inflammation, linked to what health officials here say is a lethal strain of the Coxsackie virus.

Chua urged parents throughout the country to continue to keep their young children indoors, or at least away from playgrounds, pools, daycare centres or shopping malls and other places where children gather.
The outbreak of Coxsackie has caused hundreds of cases of the relatively benign foot-and-mouth disease but has also led to the myocarditis cases in Sarawak.
Chua said 1,350 children have been admitted to hospitals throughout the country for suspected Coxsackie B and A infection of which 279 were still hospitalised.

Malaysia called in experts from Atlanta's Centre for Disease Control and Prevention earlier this month. They found traces of another virus in at least two of the victims that has no known cure or vaccine, Health ministry officials said.
Chua said on Monday that experts from Tokyo's Institute of Infectious Diseases have also arrived to help out.
Medical authorities have exchanged opinions about the virus on the Internet and the University of Nebraska Medical Centre in the United States has a web site tracking developments about the disease.
"...the identity of the virus -- if it is a virus -- that has caused the paediatric deaths remains a mystery...," the centre said in an update last week.
A lively newsgroup page has appeared on the Internet featuring scorching criticisms of how Malaysian health authorities are handling the outbreak, along with oddball theories on how to cure it.
What has puzzled health officials is why the virus is killing children in Sarawak and nowhere else in Malaysia.
